items.title: The right derived functor of the inverse limit on N-indexed abelian groups has the standard two-term representation and vanishes above degree one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the existence of the right derived functor R lim : D(Ab(N)) -> D(Ab) of the inverse limit and then lists five properties: that R^p lim vanishes for p > 1; that R lim A_n is represented by the two-term complex prod A_n -> prod A_n with the displayed map sitting in degrees 0 and 1; that for a Mittag-Leffler system R^1 lim vanishes; that every object of D(Ab(N)) is quasi-isomorphic to a complex whose terms are right acyclic for lim; and that if each K^p is right acyclic then R lim K is represented by the complex of its limits (source lines 22942-22968). The proof constructs the acyclics by hand: for an arbitrary inverse system (A_n) it forms the system (B_n) with B_n = A_n oplus A_{n-1} oplus ... oplus A_1 and transition maps the projections, and embeds A_n into B_n by the displayed tuple built from the composites of the transition maps f_i, showing that every inverse system is a subobject of a Mittag-Leffler system (proof lines 22971-22980). Using the right-acyclic-subcategory criterion together with the Mittag-Leffler lemma it follows that every Mittag-Leffler system is right acyclic for lim, which is property (3), and this already defines RF on D^+(Ab(N)) (proof lines 22981-22986). The proof then sets C_n = A_{n-1} oplus ... oplus A_1 for n > 1 and C_1 = 0 with projection transitions, obtains the short exact sequence of inverse systems 0 -> (A_n) -> (B_n) -> (C_n) -> 0 where the map B_n -> C_n is the displayed difference map, and since (C_n) is also Mittag-Leffler concludes property (2), which implies (1) (proof lines 22987-22993). Finally, the unbounded right derived functor lemma gives that R lim is defined on all of D(Ab(N)), and its proof proceeds by establishing (4) and (5) (proof lines 22994-22999). The non-routine content is the explicit embedding of an arbitrary inverse system into a Mittag-Leffler one, which is what manufactures the acyclic objects.
